books.title: Captains Courageous
books.author: Rudyard Kipling
books.desc: The spoiled son of an American millionaire falls overboard from a liner and is picked up by a fishing schooner on the Grand Banks.
about: Harvey Cheyne, a boy of about fifteen and the son of a wealthy California railroad magnate, is travelling to Europe on a transatlantic liner when he falls overboard off the Grand Banks of Newfoundland. He is rescued by the crew of the fishing schooner We're Here, from Gloucester, Massachusetts. Its captain, Disko Troop, does not believe his stories of wealth and will not cut short the fishing season, so he offers Harvey a place in the crew alongside his son Dan, Long Jack, Manuel, Salters, Penn and the others.

Kipling's novel follows Harvey's transformation through hard work, danger and comradeship at sea, and gives a detailed picture of the life of the cod fishermen of the North Atlantic. Its portrait of the ship's Black cook and some of the dialogue use the racial language of its time.
Captains Courageous was serialised in McClure's Magazine from November 1896 and published as a book in 1897.

books.title: Martin Eden
books.author: Jack London
books.desc: A young sailor from Oakland falls in love with a refined young woman and sets out to educate himself and become a writer.
about: Martin Eden, a rough young sailor from a working-class background, rescues Arthur Morse from a fight and is invited to dinner with his wealthy family in Oakland. There he meets Arthur's sister Ruth, a university student, and falls in love with her and with the world of books she represents. Determined to become worthy of her, he throws himself into self-education and resolves to earn his living as a writer, struggling against poverty and rejection, and finding a friend in the poet Brissenden.

Often described as London's most autobiographical novel, Martin Eden draws on his own struggle for education and literary success. It explores class, ambition, love and the nature of success, and London himself presented the book as an attack on individualism. Some passages reflect the racial ideas and language of its time.

Martin Eden was serialised in The Pacific Monthly from September 1908 to September 1909 and published as a book by Macmillan in 1909. Ruth Morse is said to have been modelled on Mabel Applegarth, London's first love, and Brissenden on his friend the poet George Sterling. This edition also offers the Italian translation by Gian Dàuli.

books.title: The Memoirs of Sherlock Holmes
books.author: Arthur Conan Doyle
books.desc: The second collection of Sherlock Holmes stories, from the disappearance of a racehorse to the famous struggle with Professor Moriarty.
about: In these stories Dr Watson recounts more cases of his friend Sherlock Holmes, the consulting detective of Baker Street. Holmes investigates the disappearance of the racehorse Silver Blaze and the murder of its trainer, a gruesome parcel received by a quiet lady in Croydon, and other mysteries. Watson also learns about Holmes's early life, including his first case and his brother Mycroft. The collection ends with Holmes's confrontation with Professor Moriarty, the criminal mastermind.
Conan Doyle's stories combine logical deduction, vivid characters and atmosphere, and helped to define the modern detective story.

The twelve stories first appeared in The Strand Magazine from December 1892 to December 1893 and were collected in book form at the end of 1893. The first British edition left out "The Adventure of the Cardboard Box", which the first American edition included; this edition includes it.

books.title: The First Men in the Moon
books.author: H. G. Wells
books.desc: A penniless businessman and an eccentric scientist fly to the Moon in a sphere coated with an anti-gravity substance and discover a lunar civilisation.
about: Bedford, a businessman in financial difficulty, retires to the Kent coast to write a play and meets Cavor, an absent-minded scientist who has invented Cavorite, a substance that blocks gravity. Seeing a fortune to be made, Bedford joins Cavor in building a sphere coated with it, and the two men travel to the Moon. There they discover a strange landscape and the Selenites, insect-like creatures who live in vast caverns beneath the surface and are ruled by the Grand Lunar.

Told by Bedford, the novel combines scientific adventure, humour and social satire, contrasting Bedford's greed with Cavor's pure curiosity and using the society of the Selenites to comment on human civilisation.
The First Men in the Moon was serialised in The Strand Magazine from December 1900 to August 1901, with illustrations by Claude Shepperson, and published as a book in 1901.

books.title: At the Back of the North Wind
books.author: George MacDonald
books.desc: Diamond, a poor coachman's son in London, is carried away at night by the mysterious lady North Wind and glimpses the country at her back.
about: Diamond is the son of a coachman and sleeps in a loft above the coach-house, close to the horse old Diamond, whose name he shares. One night the North Wind, who appears to him as a beautiful and sometimes frightening lady, speaks to him through a hole in the wall and begins to carry him on journeys over London and beyond. Back in the everyday world, Diamond's family faces hard times, and the gentle boy helps those around him, among them the crossing-sweeper Nanny, her friend Jim and the kind Mr Raymond.

MacDonald's book mixes fantasy and realistic scenes of poverty in Victorian London, and is full of songs, dreams and stories within the story. It reflects on goodness, suffering and death through the eyes of a child.
At the Back of the North Wind was serialised in the children's magazine Good Words for the Young from 1868 and published as a book in 1871.
